clue.text: Any number in depression squealed

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the dip that the clue calls a depression

parts.note: a sag is a dip or depression
N is the algebraic symbol for any number

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a hollow let out a squeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squealed' in the slang of informers means told on someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: an informer who squealed has turned informer, grassed to the authorities.

clue.text: Acting as guide for us, the fellow leading band

indicators.note: leading puts the earlier pieces in front of the last one

parts.note: he refers to a male person
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A bandleader escorting a group shows us the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing people to their seats or through a building is guiding them, the job of an attendant at the door.

clue.text: Shown mercy, revolutionary soldiers rushed outside

indicators.note: outside says the word for rushed is wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: sped means hurried or rushed

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the soldiers' letters go backwards

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a stock abbreviation for soldiers

explanation.surface: Captives were let off as rebel troops charged past them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone shown mercy has been let off, kept from harm or punishment.

clue.text: One sees weather coming? Take care moving into wild forest

indicators.note: into says the rearranged care goes inside the other jumble
wild suggests disorder, so the letters of forest are scrambled
moving says the letters of care shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A walker who spots a storm approaching is told to be careful heading into a dense wood.
explanation.walkthrough: Both anagram signals, 'wild' and 'moving', act on their own words; 'into' sets one jumble inside the other. 'Take' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather predictor, in a playful sense, sees what weather is on its way before it arrives.

clue.text: See 11
Summer month's upset, having an absence of fertiliser

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the month's abbreviation reads backwards

parts.note: Aug is short for August, a summer month in the north
no means none of, an absence of

explanation.surface: A garden short of manure has had a bad August.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: seabird or bat droppings are collected and spread on fields as a rich natural manure.

clue.text: It's bad — tetanus, unfortunately, is confirmed

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A doctor's grim diagnosis of lockjaw has been verified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'unfortunately' does the scrambling.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a claim that has been confirmed is backed up with proof, verified.

clue.text: Mistaken to have new leader? One has a point

indicators.note: a new leader means the first letter of the word for mistaken is swapped for another

parts.note: wrong means mistaken

explanation.surface: Someone in error is to be given a new boss, and somebody has a fair argument.
explanation.walkthrough: The new first letter P is not clued separately; 'point' hints at it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: each spike of a fork or the tine of an antler is a pointed projection.

clue.text: Knight wearing gaudy decoration

indicators.note: the word for gaudy is wearing the knight, which sits inside it

parts.note: garish means showy or gaudy
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight is dressed in flashy ornamentation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a culinary trim or embellishment added to a dish to make it look attractive.

clue.text: Hairstyle augmented by the French item of jewellery

indicators.note: augmented by means the hairstyle has the next piece added after it

parts.note: bangs are a fringe of hair cut straight across the forehead, a hairstyle
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French woman's fringe is complemented by her jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a rigid bracelet worn on the wrist is a piece of jewellery.

clue.text: Shrub man with special pole found by railway

indicators.note: found by says the railway piece sits next to the man with the pole

parts.note: a barber traditionally has a striped pole outside the shop

explanation.surface: A bush is discovered beside a railway line, together with a man carrying a strange pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a thorny bush with yellow flowers and red berries, grown in hedges and gardens.

clue.text: Elder assessing tot in difficulty — reason for optimism?

indicators.note: in difficulty says the letters are in trouble, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grandparent sizing up a struggling toddler hopes for the best.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as playful: the phrase is about a cheery outlook, not literal eyewear.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: looking through spectacles tinted pink makes everything look better, hence an over-hopeful view.

clue.text: Head of enterprise talked about workplace being expanded

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of enterprise

parts.note: a lab is a laboratory, a scientist's workplace
orated means held forth, talked; about is a link meaning on the subject of

explanation.surface: The boss of a firm gave a speech about the office being enlarged.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a point that has been expanded is developed in more detail, filled out.

clue.text: Completely dry? You'll find some bar ideal

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A teetotaller finds an alcohol-free pub perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'You'll find', but those words are only a link to the wordplay; 'Completely dry' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: land without any moisture at all, like a desert, is parched through and through.

clue.text: Anglicans might get upset? No need for one prolonged row!

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of anglicans might are rearranged
no need for says the numeral for one is not used in the rearrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Church of England members may be offended, but a long quarrel is unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles ANGLICANS MIGHT, and 'No need for one' drops an I from that pool, leaving thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a long exchange of abuse and insults is a drawn-out quarrel.

clue.text: Works hard penning article — choice phrases required?

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the article goes inside

parts.note: slogs means toils, works hard
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A writer toils over a piece, needing well-chosen words.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: catchy mottoes used in advertising or politics are pithy, carefully chosen phrases.

clue.text: Suspicion of haze, result of dampness

parts.note: mist is a light haze
rust forms on iron left damp

explanation.surface: A fog is distrusted as the outcome of damp weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lack of trust, doubt about someone's honesty.

clue.text: Sitting by river see sport

indicators.note: sitting by says the two pieces are placed side by side

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Sitting at the riverside you can watch a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a team game played on horseback with mallets and a ball.

clue.text: Normal 'mister', a man out of the ordinary?

indicators.note: out of the ordinary means unusual, so these letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Is a mere 'mister' an extraordinary fellow?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays the definition 'Normal' against 'out of the ordinary'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: conventional, in line with what most people think or do.

clue.text: It's miserable, suffering from a disease in childhood?

definitions.meaning: miserable here means paltry or meagre

definitions.text: suffering from a disease in childhood?
definitions.meaning: literally, having a common childhood illness with a red rash

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal second reading of the word as 'having the measles'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in the first sense: a stingy, contemptibly small amount; the second reads the word literally as spotty with illness.

clue.text: Knowing there's a conflict over recreational drug

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the earlier pieces sit above the drug

parts.note: a war is an armed conflict
E is short for ecstasy, a recreational drug

explanation.surface: Someone has learned of a fight over party pills.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being conscious of something, informed about it.

clue.text: Big flow of water about needing a sailor to do something

parts.note: ca is short for circa, about
tar is an old word for a sailor
act means to take action, do something

explanation.surface: A flood about which a seaman must take action.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a large waterfall or torrent of water.

clue.text: Hesitation about meat presented in show

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the hesitation's letters are reversed

parts.note: er is a sound of hesitation
veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: A cook hesitates over the meat at a food show.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to uncover or disclose, display something hidden.

clue.text: Hide in depression, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard said rather than seen written

parts.note: a vale is a valley, a depression in the land

explanation.surface: Someone takes cover in a hollow, as rumour has it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to cover up or conceal, as a cloth screen does a face.

clue.text: Start of sunny spring? Smashing!

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of sunny

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: A sunny start to spring is a delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated slang synonym: an exclamation meaning excellent or great.

clue.text: Left-looking journalist with nastiness for all

indicators.note: looking left means reading right to left, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: ed is short for editor, a journalist
spite is malice, nastiness

explanation.surface: A left-wing journalist shows malice to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for all' reads like 'towards everyone' but means 'in spite of', as in 'for all his efforts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: in phrases such as 'for all his talk', the words mean notwithstanding.
